findings.claim: Paragraph 4 states that over the decade 'every number the ridge keeps got worse together', which contradicts paragraphs 2-3, where one of the two ridge records explicitly improved over the same ten seasons.
findings.evidence: P2: 'Across the ten seasons since the code passed, the zenith reading improved by about three percent.' P3: '...which is how a slightly better zenith number and twenty-three lost nights ended up describing the same ten seasons.' P4: 'at Ashcombe, thirty kilometers down the valley, no code was ever adopted, uplight rose through the same decade, and every number the ridge keeps got worse together.' The passage names exactly two ridge series (the zenith photometer reading and the faint-galaxy night count); paragraph 3's whole point is that they moved in OPPOSITE directions across the decade, so a blanket 'every number the ridge keeps got worse together' about 'the same decade' cannot be literally true.
findings.why: The integrated stage's remit is cross-paragraph reconciliation ('a number that won't reconcile', self-contradiction). This is a genuine reconciliation failure on the unit's two headline series, and the Q3 rationale leans on the very sentence at issue ('The same monitoring is what establishes the Ashcombe result, where "every number the ridge keeps got worse together"'), so a student who spots the clash finds the WHY-NOT-C rebuttal weakened. Kept minor rather than verdict-changing because (a) paragraph 4 does establish that the photometer yields directional/spectral numbers beyond the zenith ('the north horizon brightens and the ratio of red to blue ... shifts'), leaving a charitable reading in which 'every number' means the numbers bearing on that direction, and (b) the fix is a one-clause qualification. Key D for Q3 survives regardless: the passage independently names two confounds that 'would move a three percent figure' each on its own.

findings.claim: Q1 key C over-scopes 'installed output' from street lighting to the town as a whole, importing the exact totality error that the unit itself teaches against.
findings.evidence: Option C: 'Almost all of it is shielded now, and the town's total installed output has come down.' The passage licenses only: 'Ninety-four percent of the street lighting is now full cutoff. The installed output is down about a fifth since the code passed' — a street-lighting figure. Paragraph 4 then establishes an unlit-by-the-code source that is inside the town: 'Two hectares of greenhouse at the north edge of town are lit through the winter nights ... and the code was never written to reach them.' The passage never quantifies the greenhouse's output, so 'the town's total installed output' is not established.
findings.why: The unit's thesis is that the town-level tally is not total ('The units were poles'), and Q1's own distractor A is punished for exactly this scope move ('The code covers private fixtures as well as poles'). The key should not itself say 'the town's total'. Not verdict-changing: the Q1 stem frames the question as 'Brackwell's street lighting', so within that frame C reads as the street-lighting total and the other three options are plainly false — C remains the single best answer and is defensible to a complaining student. Note also that the candidates-final correction pass edited this same option ('Nearly all' -> 'Almost all') without touching 'the town's total'.

findings.claim: The Q4 rationale's evidence chain commits a soft version of the attribution swap it labels as distractor B's trap.
findings.evidence: Rationale: 'WHY-KEY (A): the concession is made in the text's own voice and made flatly — Feltrin "grants him the half she thinks is his, and grants it without hedging"'. The quoted clause is an attribution to Feltrin, not the narrator. The rationale then labels B 'trap: role_or_attribution_swap — the TYPE-005 signature ... A solver reading for tone rather than for the speaker hands it to the writer'.
findings.why: In a stance item whose whole teaching payload is 'track the speaker, not the tone', the rationale offers a character's concession as proof of the writer's voice. It does recover in the next clause by citing the genuinely narratorial sentence ('the passage adds its own verdict sentence, "Where the fixtures are unshielded the fixtures are the story."'), so key A is correctly supported and the verdict stands; the defect is in the teaching text, not the key.

findings.claim: Local dependence: three distractors across three different questions are all falsified by the same single fact, so one retrieval win propagates.
findings.evidence: Q1 key C ('the town's total installed output has come down'), Q2 distractor C ('They put less total light over the valley than the shielded fixtures that took their place'), and Q5 distractor D ('the total light over the valley kept rising through the decade') all turn on the one clause 'The installed output is down about a fifth since the code passed' / 'in total no brighter'. A solver who answers the easy paragraph-1 retrieval (Q1) can eliminate Q2 C and Q5 D without re-reading.
findings.why: Pedagogy's remit includes whether a solver can score above chance without the work the item is meant to measure. The recorded G-STEM flag already noted the Q5 half of this ('A and D rest on the same underlying claim that light over the valley rose through the decade'), but the cross-question propagation from Q1's key was not recorded. Minor rather than verdict-changing: eliminating one distractor still leaves two substantive alternatives in each of Q2 and Q5, and the keys there (B, C) require passage-specific content the fact does not supply.
